title: Embeddable libraries and integration closure
body:
## Current memory/continuity contract — 2026-10-11

Laputa remains the owning library for cognitive/ACTMEM semantics; VIVY owns unified context admission and execution. [VIVY #58](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/58) owns the new continuity/Recap/UI design, coordinated with [VIVY #57](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/57) for subjects and workers.

- VIVY owns the foundational capability in its **unified context pipeline**. LIFE is the first default-enabled pilot once delivered; coding-agent compositions/CODE remain excluded from phase-one resident-Recap admission.
- All VIVY-owned persistent sessions share **one subject-level, free-form ACTMEM Recap**, fully visible/editable through its owning UI/API. This is not a per-session Recap. Delegated role-only workers retain scoped task history and receive neither persona nor the subject Recap automatically; access requires explicit trusted scope/permissions.
- Persist raw source evidence continuously. Commit the replacement Recap revision and covered-source references before unloading retiring raw context, keep it stable between consolidation points, and preserve recoverable revisions/provenance. Numeric budgets/thresholds remain design/tuning choices.
- Forgetting is **explicit and targeted**: guide the human to delete/edit ACTMEM in the UI, or execute the selected backend's authorized deletion tool (for example BML) when requested. Do not automatically cascade/purge other stores or equate context removal with erasure. Preserve existing provider-owned index consistency/tombstone/replay guarantees within the selected operation.
- ACTMEM agent-management tools are required, normally hidden/deferred-discovery/on-demand. The exact discovery mechanism remains a design choice; their complete schemas need not be exposed in every ordinary turn.
- Initial validation targets **BML**; the owner will test **Mentle through DIVA**. Maintain full compatibility through the shared abstract CRUD/search contract. Providers own concrete returns, storage, indexing and ranking; VIVY owns authorized scope, context admission and budgets. No implicit backend replacement, dual write or migration.
- Explicit must-not-forget content should guide the human to **Laputa's frozen layer using the existing human-controlled review/edit path**. Recap consolidation/ordinary editing or pinning cannot automatically mutate Persona, Mission or Dream or gain new governance authority.

Current source still has Pulse/Recap/Work and scoped consumers. Plan compatibility for their capture/reconcile/review/strategy/UI contracts before implementing the Recap-only direction; this update does not change runtime schemas, erase state or claim delivery. Preserve existing embedded/domain/human-controlled facade foundations and original M4/M5/S12 scope. The older proposal and comment remain historical at their recorded revisions. VIVY standalone integration #17 remains cancelled; no new memory default, backend replacement or migration is inferred.

## Reopened status — 2026-10-04 20:04 (Asia/Shanghai)

**Open independent proposal / plan / unfinished capability tracker.** The owner clarified that unimplemented feature ideas and plans must remain open in their original issues. The earlier consolidation closure is superseded; this issue again owns its pending feature scope. Opening the issue does not schedule coding, approve a dependency/default switch or establish product acceptance.

### Latest recorded implementation boundary

Explicit paths, pure-Go canonical/KG storage and public Garden composition already exist. #2 delivered Mission/scoped ACTMEM/DIVA strategy/capture foundations; #3 delivered embedded domain/human facade. The old rebuild/REST-only/no-facade assumptions are obsolete. Remaining injectable embedding/logger/remote modes, model/module release decisions, selected-backend/conformance and Garden INOFY S12 work remain tracked here; no default memory replacement is approved.

Evidence above is carried from the earlier status reconciliation; this reopening is an issue-management change, not a fresh source/test certification. Preserve already delivered components and previously deferred ownership.

[#31](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/31) remains the cross-project delivered-system closure tracker. It links to this feature issue instead of replacing it. Original comments are retained.

<details>
<summary>Original proposal and requirements (retained; current boundary above takes precedence)</summary>

## Summary

Proposal: make the MemPalace memory store (mentle) a properly detachable library, so hosts like `agent-vivy` can embed it in-process instead of running a separate backend service. Garden's HTTP server and mentle's MCP server become *optional protocol adapters* rather than mandatory deployment pieces.

## Motivation

- **agent-diva legacy**: agent-diva (Rust) could not consume the Go mentle, so it re-implemented memory storage in-repo as BML (typed SQLite + FTS5). The old path accumulated dual authorities (`Persona JSON ↔ BML`), double ledgers (`governance.db` + `governance.sqlite3`), and a residual `memory_md` chain, and had to be removed in a one-time cognitive clean break (S5). The Rust rewrite is also a capability downgrade: no vector/semantic search, no hybrid retrieval, no temporal KG, no WAL. A detachable Go library means no host ever has to re-implement memory again.
- **agent-vivy fit**: vivy is Go, so it *can* embed mentle directly. Vivy's single-organism model (one process, one Journal lease) favors an in-process memory module over a permanent sidecar on `127.0.0.1:7373`. Vivy's `std/context-source@v1` port + ContextHost is the natural seam — SCX already reserves a Memory context-source slot.
- **What "no mempalace backend" means**: the backend becomes optional, not deleted. Non-Go hosts still need an adapter (MCP stdio or HTTP).

## Non-goal

Do not merge memory tables into vivy's `core/storage-engine` contract. Memory ≠ Journal; mentle's storage semantics (HNSW / KG / WAL / canonical catalog) are not isomorphic to the journal contracts. The palace data dir can live under vivy's data dir for unified backup, but the storage stacks stay separate.

## Work items

### mentle — embeddability gaps

1. `facade.Init` currently hardwires the hugot embedder, govector store, and viper config loading. Extend `facade.Options` to inject `PalacePath` / `ModelsDir` / `Embedder` / `Logger` directly (no hard dependency on `~/.mempalace/config.json`).
2. Abstract the embedder behind an interface with three modes: local ONNX (hugot), OpenAI-compatible remote, none (lexical-only). This controls binary size and CGO surface for hosts.
3. Replace `mattn/go-sqlite3` (CGO) in `facade/canonical.go` and `storage/sqlite/store.go` with `modernc.org/sqlite`, or make the driver configurable — embedding mentle into vivy's pure-Go build must not reintroduce CGO.
4. Decide ONNX model distribution: bundle vs. on-demand download vs. build-tag variant without embeddings.

### garden — split shell from semantics

5. Extract the semantic layer (`internal/recall`: fast/deep/rank/trace; `internal/activity`: session lifecycle, idempotent session end, working set) into an importable package — either a `garden`-core library or down into mentle. The HTTP `main.go` should become a thin routing shell.
6. Keep the HTTP server and mentle MCP server as maintained adapters for non-Go hosts (Claude Desktop/Cursor and future Rust hosts).

### versioning

7. mentle is a separate Go module (`github.com/dashimaki/mentle`); define tag/release policy so hosts can pin versions.

## Phases

- **Phase 0 (laputa)**: items 1–6.
- **Phase 1 (agent-vivy)**: new module `vivy/memory-laputa` implementing `std/context-source@v1` (read direction) plus optional authorized experience write-back; config `memory.backend: off | embedded | remote`; palace data under `{vivy data}/memory/`.
- **Phase 2 (agent-diva payoff)**: diva can consume the same implementation via the MCP/HTTP adapter — no third memory implementation.

## Evidence

- `mentle/facade` is already the only public seam (`internal/` layout enforces it); public methods: `SearchCards`, `ReadEvidence`, `CreateMemory`/`Get`/`Update`/`Delete`/`ListMemories`, `Write`/`Read`/`List`/`Forget`, `Retrieve`, `QueryEntity`, `Timeline`, `ListCollections`.
- vivy's storage: `internal/storage` contracts + sqlite (modernc, pure Go) + postgres backends behind conformance suite; organism lease = single-writer model.
- SCX (`agent-vivy/docs/architecture/SCX-ARCHITECTURE-DESIGN.md`) names laputa-garden an intended integration partner; MEM-1 is deferred pending exactly this kind of direction.

[Written by Devin](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/43bc761c2f7b44c2990d28245ae8d83f)



</details>

## Follow-up proposal: close the remaining Laputa / ViVy / INOFY integration work

The next step is to finish and connect the existing implementations, not rebuild a memory system or workflow engine. This proposal updates the execution order for this issue after the embeddability work and INOFY development.

### Evidence baseline

Source snapshots inspected:

- Laputa: `384d54d3a5b98dc00e9c87bcd359c8d55c7ab5ad`.
- agent-vivy: `5347032d8f18a047b67e85761c0dcc48728bee7c`.
- INOFY: `71e2c9bbe47d5d095b27d756e38eaff565d93d36`.

Relevant contracts and records:

- [ADR-0016: embeddable libraries and modular monolith](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/384d54d3a5b98dc00e9c87bcd359c8d55c7ab5ad/docs/architecture/0016-laputa-embeddable-modular-monolith.md).
- [Laputa implementation baseline and open M4/M5 gates](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/384d54d3a5b98dc00e9c87bcd359c8d55c7ab5ad/docs/bmad/laputa-modular-monolith-2026-09/README.md).
- [Vivy handoff, including the evidence-scope limitation](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/384d54d3a5b98dc00e9c87bcd359c8d55c7ab5ad/docs/bmad/laputa-modular-monolith-2026-09/vivy-handoff.md).
- [ViVy workflow follow-up index](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/21): PR #24 is merged; its older WF-1/WF-2 rebuilding checklist is superseded.
- [ViVy dependency pin](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/blob/5347032d8f18a047b67e85761c0dcc48728bee7c/go.mod): INOFY is already pinned to `71e2c9bbe47d`.
- [INOFY S12: real Garden Fast/Deep adapters](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/INOFY/blob/71e2c9bbe47d5d095b27d756e38eaff565d93d36/docs/superpowers/plans/inofy/S12.md).

These are source and historical implementation records, not a fresh full-suite certification. No new product implementation or test rerun is claimed by this comment.

### What should not be implemented again

| Original issue area | Current baseline | Remaining obligation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit palace/model paths | Implemented | Preserve ambient-config isolation and host-owned absolute paths. |
| Embedding/config injection | Partial: strict local-model startup and lexical degradation exist | Finish the injectable embedding/logging boundary and the requested remote embedding mode; prove truthful mode capabilities. |
| Pure-Go SQLite | Implemented in canonical/KG and Garden state stores | Revalidate the actual ViVy dependency closure and build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`. |
| Model distribution | Deployment decision remains | Specify packaging/offline behavior; no implicit download during embedded startup. |
| Importable Garden semantics | `garden/agentapi` and shared `internal/runtimecore` exist | Finish policy/conformance; do not copy these services into ViVy. |
| REST/MCP adapters | Maintained; some embedded/REST fixtures exist | Complete equivalence for advertised capabilities, not speculative bootstrap/capture support. |
| Versioning | Local importability is demonstrated using sibling/local replacements | Resolve module identity, nested-module tag policy, compatibility and independent-consumer evidence. Public publication remains separately authorized. |

ViVy already has a wired BML memory provider. That is not a Laputa integration. Likewise, the independent `examples/vivy-embed-smoke` consumer is not proof that ViVy has adopted Laputa.

ADR-0016 refines the old ADR-0015 REST-only in-process/default-transport decision. REST remains the canonical wire profile; embedded and wire calls must share domain rules. Do not restart the older REST-first worktree as if ADR-0016 did not exist.

### Intended outcome

- A ViVy user can explicitly select a Laputa-backed integration without requiring a permanently running Garden sidecar, without losing or implicitly merging existing BML data.
- The Agent receives bounded, correctly scoped context before a model request. Guessing a card ID or supplying a scope in model-authored input cannot grant evidence access.
- Durable terminal events can be captured idempotently and inspected after restart. Accepted delivery, completed canonical ingestion and derived-index health remain distinct.
- Non-Go hosts retain REST/MCP adapters with the same tested policy and domain semantics.
- Garden uses the existing INOFY engine for actual recall orchestration without inventing a second scheduler or ingestion queue.

### Proposed work packages

#### A. Establish execution baselines and reconcile status

- [ ] Select pinned upstream baselines and isolated worktrees for Laputa and ViVy; inventory and protect unrelated local changes.
- [ ] Reconcile this issue, M1-M5, INOFY S11/S12/S13 and the ViVy memory/workflow trackers against actual source and acceptance records.
- [ ] Treat the old dirty `garden-laputa-agent-sdk` worktree as candidate owned hunks, not already integrated code; do not reset, clean or implicitly merge it.

Acceptance: downstream tasks reference immutable source and do not repeat completed pure-Go storage, domain extraction or ViVy INOFY cutover work.

#### B. Enforce evidence authorization before exposing untrusted references

This is the first product safety gate. Current `garden/agentapi/reads.go` authorizes the operation and bounds its budgets, then calls Mentle evidence expansion by card ID. Search scope is a query filter, not per-card authorization. The handoff explicitly records this limitation.

- [ ] Freeze the mapping from host-owned profile/agent/workspace/session identity to allowed memory scopes. Missing mappings must deny, not silently widen.
- [ ] Enforce that policy at search, explicit expansion and automatic recall; apply the required validity/status policy before returning evidence.
- [ ] Add negative tests for cross-scope IDs, forged/conflicting bindings, disallowed or expired records and scope drift between discovery and expansion, alongside legitimate reads and budget tests.

Acceptance: a valid Agent principal cannot bypass its allowed evidence boundary merely by knowing an ID. This does not claim that all existing authorization is absent.

#### C. Finish the library and transport boundary

- [ ] Complete the issue-requested embedding injection/modes and logging boundary using existing components where suitable; test local/remote/unavailable behavior without paid live calls.
- [ ] Preserve the current no-model contract: lexical mode over an existing canonical database is read-only; queued capture is not a successful canonical write. Corrupt local models must not trigger an invisible download/fallback.
- [ ] Run shared positive/negative fixtures through embedded and REST calls, and through MCP for the capabilities it actually implements. Advertise only executable, tested capabilities.
- [ ] Define module-path/tag compatibility and model packaging decisions; prove an independent consumer build without relying solely on a developer checkout's sibling `replace` directives. Do not publish remotely as a side effect.

Acceptance: shared bindings, budgets, typed failures, frozen context, capture replay/conflict and restart/degradation behavior are proven for the advertised surface; pure-Go support is checked on the final dependency graph.

#### D. Implement the real ViVy host bridge

Use `garden/agentapi`, not direct Mentle storage or Garden internals.

- [ ] Map the integration through existing Modules/Ports and ContextHost/ObserverHost/ActionHost seams, preserving the one `Service.Run` / Journal / Policy path.
- [ ] Bind trusted host identity and session; obtain bounded recall before the first model request. Persona instruction projection belongs in the Host-owned admitted prompt snapshot, not in an arbitrary required context candidate.
- [ ] Preserve session-frozen six-slot Persona projection and committed resume snapshots. WORLD, ACTMEM and history remain explicit-only. Required identity failure must not silently substitute a different persona.
- [ ] Capture only after the host Journal durably records an authorized terminal event. Reuse existing observer delivery/cursor machinery where sufficient; separate host redelivery responsibility from Garden's existing durable ingest processing rather than adding duplicate queues.
- [ ] Surface accepted/completed/pending/failed states and index lag truthfully through existing tools/status/Memory and Persona surfaces.
- [ ] Enforce one primary write destination per scope. Additional sources may be read mounts; selecting Laputa must not imply default BML replacement, migration or dual writes.

Acceptance: real ViVy request-before-model ordering, terminal-only capture, duplicate replay, changed-content conflict, unavailable backend, frozen persona and restart recovery pass; run ViVy `just ci`, both applicable storage conformance paths and real-path smoke.

#### E. Complete Garden's INOFY S12 consumption

- [ ] Capture behavior fixtures from live `FastService.Recall` and `DeepService.Recall`, not only a dormant pipeline YAML implementation.
- [ ] Extract narrow trusted domain nodes and route the existing service entries through INOFY. Reuse its pinned Eino-based compiler/runtime; no replacement scheduler or Agent loop.
- [ ] Preserve card-before-evidence, six-slot Frozen Core, WORLD/ACTMEM exclusion, output types, warning/degradation semantics, budgets and trace provenance. Normalize only trace IDs/timestamps in equivalence tests.
- [ ] Keep synchronous read-only recall on the explicit ephemeral RunStore contract; do not advertise crash-resumable waits. Delegate ingestion effects and original event identity to Garden's existing receipt/idempotency service.

Acceptance: real Fast/Deep service parity, planner-absent/failure and bounded-evidence negative cases pass; ingestion replay returns the existing receipt and conflicting payload is rejected. No second ingestion queue.

#### F. Joint acceptance and delivery closure

- [ ] Run the mandatory Laputa/Mentle/Garden module suites with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, Garden e2e and independent-consumer smoke; build Console assets before embed-dependent Garden tests.
- [ ] Run ViVy `just ci`, actual packaged/runtime integration and the applicable SQLite/PostgreSQL cases; a skipped driver case is not a pass.
- [ ] Record happy and failure paths for missing/corrupt models, denied scopes, unavailable providers, pending indexes, terminal replay and restart. Distinguish mock-provider from live-provider evidence.
- [ ] Update trackers and acceptance records only from observed results. Keep public publication, dependency/default switches and destructive operations behind explicit owner approval.

### Dependency order

```text
A: baselines/status
  -> B: authorization
  -> C: library/transport closure
  -> D: real ViVy integration
  -> F: joint acceptance

After A and the relevant B/C contracts stabilize:
  E: Garden/INOFY S12 can run in an isolated parallel lane -> F
```

Owners: Laputa repository owns B/C and Garden S12 changes; agent-vivy owns its native adapter, host policy/storage and product surfaces; INOFY owns generic graph semantics and upstream engine fixes. Shared interfaces are frozen before parallel writes; shared-file integration is serial.

### Related but not blocking this memory integration

ViVy issue #21 already identifies editor launch ownership and node-input authoring defects (V1/V2); those can be addressed in their own product lane. Agent access to published workflows and expanded graph/wait/persistent-child capabilities require their scoped contracts, not blanket authorization here. INOFY S13 standalone App packaging/release evidence remains a separate closure item and must not force a rebuild of the merged ViVy cutover.

### Guardrails and execution policy

- Tests-first for regression, authorization and behavior-parity work; each package needs agent-executable happy/failure QA and evidence.
- No new memory authority in the ViVy Journal, no direct authority/storage bypass, and no automatic WORLD/ACTMEM injection.
- No automatic data migration/deletion, BML replacement, default deployment switch, paid service activation, public listener or module publication.
- Preserve EvoMap ownership of capability artifacts; no new Skill-installation path in Laputa or INOFY.
- This is a submitted planning proposal, not a claim of completed implementation or completed formal plan review. Scope and architecture/distribution decisions should be reviewed before execution.

The owner-requested MENTLE upstream enhancement plan is tracked in [#7](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/issues/7). It sequences source-ingestion correctness, multilingual lexical retrieval, truthful backup/restore, source-preserving search deduplication, temporal fact replacement and optional reviewed organization repair. Existing canonical/revision/outbox and provider contracts remain authoritative. Embedder/backend expansion is coordinated with this issue, not a duplicate replacement effort; experimental multimodal/coordination features are deferred. This is a plan, not an implementation or migration start.

title: MENTLE enhancement plan: adopt implemented MemPalace Python capabilities
body:
## Status and objective

**Owner-requested enhancement plan — not an implementation start or completion claim.**

Comprehensively improve MENTLE by adapting a selected batch of capabilities already implemented in the Python MemPalace upstream. Deliver in small, independently verifiable batches; preserve MENTLE's canonical authority and existing provider abstraction.

“Implemented upstream” means inspected executable source, not proof of production maturity, benchmark superiority or compatibility with MENTLE. Distinguish published-release functionality from develop-only changes and experimental features.

## Baselines and evidence

Source audit on 2026-10-11:
- MENTLE: `ProjectViVy/laputa@4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24`.
- Python upstream: `MemPalace/mempalace@1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9`, default `develop`; source version 3.11.0.
- Latest published GitHub release observed: [v3.10.0](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/releases/tag/v3.10.0). [Release-to-inspected-source comparison](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/compare/v3.10.0...1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9).
- Related Go source family: [argylelabcoat/MemPalace-Go@89e6d982](https://github.com/argylelabcoat/MemPalace-Go/commit/89e6d9825c4bd396eb149cbc9f02c38bcced790a), whose latest observed commit is April 10 with no releases. Many inherited features are already present in MENTLE; this is not a wholesale Go-upstream catch-up.

Re-pin revisions and review upstream license/attribution before importing code. The findings below are static-source observations; no runtime reproduction or matched benchmark was performed during this research.

## Non-negotiable boundaries

- Keep MENTLE canonical records, revisions, mutation receipts, scope checks and transactional index outbox as the authority; vectors/BM25 remain derived projections.
- Preserve the shared memory CRUD/search capability contract. Backends own storage, ranking and concrete returned materials; consumers own authorized scope and context admission.
- No second production memory database, implicit dual write, backend replacement or automatic data migration.
- Reuse current embedding identity, rebuild, retrieval, ingestion and UI infrastructure. Do not rebuild capabilities already present.
- Separate standalone-library capability, exposed facade capability, Garden binding and actual VIVY/DIVA use. File presence alone is not integration.
- Coordinate document extraction with [VIVY #61](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/61), and external sources/Obsidian with [VIVY #63](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/63). MENTLE owns ingestion/storage semantics, not a duplicate office-document engine in VIVY internal.
- [VIVY #58](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/58) owns unified context/ACTMEM continuity; this plan does not introduce another Recap authority or make every enhancement a prerequisite for that work.
- Research metrics such as retrieval recall@5 are not end-to-end answer accuracy. Require matched evaluation before claiming better retrieval.

## Batch A — correctness and truthful capabilities

### A1. Lossless source/conversation ingestion

Adapt upstream's lossless splitting and versioned re-ingest behavior:
- Preserve leading text, Markdown separators, short meaningful units, turn roles/order and oversize fragments.
- Retain stable source identity, source range and parser/chunker version.
- Make re-ingestion idempotent; a chunker-version upgrade must not silently duplicate sources or discard manual changes.
- Preserve existing Garden live capture; distinguish it from offline transcript/project import.
- Reproduce and disposition the legacy Claude parser's unsupported Go regexp lookahead before declaring the importer usable.
- Verify short-chunk loss and multi-import-path duplicates rather than assuming inherited importers are complete.

Evidence: [Python lossless-ingest change](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/commit/66a354bf718ff89952140bb45d677581aba52753), [MENTLE legacy parser](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/mentle/internal/miner/convo_miner.go#L59-L95), [source identity](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/source_identity.py).

Acceptance: fixtures for short/long/multilingual conversations, separators and preambles, repeated imports, changed chunker versions, missing/swapped source directories, partial failures and restart. Prove content coverage and stable source provenance.

### A2. Chinese and multilingual lexical retrieval

This is a MENTLE correctness prerequisite, not a claim that Python upstream already solves the exact problem.
- Current BM25 tokenizer accepts only ASCII letters/digits/underscore.
- Define and test Chinese/mixed-script tokenization, normalization and query behavior.
- Ensure the no-embedding lexical fallback remains genuinely useful for the owner's Chinese workload.
- Preserve English/code identifier behavior and bounded query cost.

Evidence: [current tokenizer](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/mentle/internal/bm25/bm25.go#L223-L250).

Acceptance: Chinese-only, mixed Chinese/English, identifiers, punctuation and empty-query tests; lexical-only and hybrid evaluation recorded separately.

### A3. Real backup/restore and honest capability reporting

Legacy MCP backup/restore/sync handlers currently return text without performing the named operation. Reproduce this boundary and remove misleading success semantics.
- Implement consistent, versioned backup/restore through owning storage APIs, including canonical data and required metadata.
- Define what is reconstructible versus included; verify restore with row/content checks and rebuilt indexes.
- Include integrity checks, interrupted-write behavior, compatibility and retention policy.
- Remote sync can remain explicitly unsupported; do not label a stub as delivered.
- Restore must not silently overwrite live data or imply approval for destructive replacement.

Evidence: [Python backups](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/backups.py), [repair and verification](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/repair.py#L467-L622), [MENTLE legacy handlers](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/mentle/cmd/server/main.go#L1094-L1140).

## Batch B — retrieval usefulness and provenance

### B1. Cross-source duplicate-result folding

Adapt Python's grouping of identical passages across different sources while retaining additional locations.
- Fold presentation/ranking candidates, not canonical source identities.
- Return the best-ranked representative plus other authorized locations/provenance.
- Do not over-collapse tiny boilerplate or legitimate repeats within one source.
- Apply authorization before grouping; never disclose an inaccessible duplicate source.
- Expose truncation/completeness when widening the candidate pool is capped.

Evidence: [Python candidates](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/searcher/candidates.py#L260-L311).

Acceptance: repeated documents do not occupy all useful top-k slots; all permitted sources remain traceable; cross-scope, revision and tombstone cases stay correct.

### B2. Source/date filters and bounded bulk access

Adapt useful convenience features without copying the entire upstream tool catalog:
- Distinguish event/source time, capture time and validity time before exposing date filters.
- Add batch read/delete only if consumer needs justify them, preserving per-target scope, expected revisions and truthful partial outcomes.
- Add accurate read-only/destructive capability metadata to supported MCP surfaces.
- Reuse paged cards/evidence and existing canonical mutations.

Evidence: [Python search schemas](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/mcp_server/schemas.py).

### B3. Optional derived source-summary retrieval

Evaluate Python closet/source-summary ranking as an optional derived aid:
- Summary hits locate original evidence, not replace its authority.
- Propagate source updates/deletions to derived summaries.
- Preserve MENTLE's existing RRF design unless matched tests justify changing it.
- Legacy concatenate-and-truncate helpers must not be described as semantic summarization.

Evidence: [Python closet generation](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/closet_llm.py), [MENTLE legacy compression](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/mentle/cmd/server/main.go#L562-L595).

Acceptance: comparable corpus/chunking/model/top-k/evidence budget; measure answer usefulness, provenance correctness, latency and cost, not only recall.

## Batch C — temporal facts and organization maintenance

### C1. Atomic temporal fact supersession

MENTLE already has temporal KG primitives. Add the missing coherent replacement operation rather than another graph system:
- Close the old fact and open the replacement atomically with provenance.
- Define interval boundaries consistently; avoid both old/new facts being current at the transition.
- Support expected revision/state checks and idempotent replay.
- Keep graph-fact semantics distinct from ordinary memory-record revision semantics.

Evidence: [Python supersede](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/knowledge_graph.py#L375-L469), [MENTLE time query](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/mentle/internal/kg/knowledge_graph.go#L189-L225).

### C2. Read-only organization audit and reviewed repair

Adapt upstream diagnostics for poor grouping, naming drift, dangling links and inconsistent predicates.
- Start with actionable read-only reports; heuristic organization scores are not retrieval-quality proof.
- Later add reviewed, resumable classification/taxonomy repair with dry-run by default.
- Preserve manual organization and source identity.
- All mutations must go through canonical authority. Current content/tags-only updates do not justify bypassing authority to patch vector metadata.
- Prefer stable source/project normalization to copying all palace metaphor machinery.

Evidence: [audit](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/palace_audit.py), [room proposals/apply](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/rooms.py), [wing split](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/wing_split.py).

Acceptance: stale-plan rejection, manual classifications retained, cancel/restart/replay, no lost records/provenance and no cross-scope moves.

## Batch D — optional extension after core evidence

### Configurable embedders and storage adapters

Evaluate actual Python backend/model adapters against [Laputa #1](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/issues/1)'s existing ownership. Avoid duplicate plans.
- Capability negotiation, vector dimension/model identity, explicit re-embedding and offline behavior.
- Add only selected providers with conformance tests; never silently mix embedding spaces.
- MENTLE already has model identity, rebuilds and lexical fallback; extend rather than replace them.

[Python backend registry](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/1f0803a31958b30320418356b2db88c4ed9c27f9/mempalace/backends/registry.py).

### Deferred experimental track

EmbeddingGemma 2 native media/code retrieval, broad multi-agent logstream coordination and full upstream MCP/PQL catalog parity are **not core-batch prerequisites**. Upstream media support is experimental/file-level and lacks several lifecycle/segment features. Record interest separately rather than describing it as mature required parity.

[Media feature](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/commit/55ed1df4faabfda69dcf53adfef3fd29cba38609).

## Delivery and review gates

- [ ] Refresh the feature matrix: upstream implemented/released/experimental, MENTLE already present/missing/placeholder, exposed versus wired.
- [ ] Reproduce static correctness findings with focused tests before claiming runtime failures.
- [ ] Deliver Batch A in small changes, preserving current authority and consumer compatibility.
- [ ] Deliver B/C features independently with precise provider contracts and feature-specific tests.
- [ ] Verify canonical/version/scope/tombstone/replay guarantees after each batch.
- [ ] Document backward compatibility and any migration separately; no silent re-ingest or destructive restore.
- [ ] Evaluate Chinese and mixed-language retrieval, duplicates, source corrections/deletions, unavailable embeddings, recovery and bounded resource use.
- [ ] Report local library tests, Garden binding tests and VIVY/DIVA product validation separately.
- [ ] Keep optional expansion out of the critical path and reuse existing work in Laputa #1 / VIVY #4.
- [ ] Publish honest capability/status documentation: no response-only tool counted as implemented, no source-only feature counted as integrated.

The owner requested this plan to collect and sequence useful upstream enhancements. Filing it does not authorize all optional features, implementation sessions, runtime changes, data migrations or deployment.
author: mastwet

title: Standalone multi-persona memory: private by default, explicit sharing, minimal first release
body:
## Status and owner direction

Owner-requested proposal, scoped on 2026-10-12. **Prioritize directly useful product behavior and the smallest coherent implementation. Keep useful existing mechanisms; defer optional security hardening and speculative infrastructure.**

The earlier broad architecture review is research input, not a requirement to implement every recommendation. This issue records a lean first-release direction; it does not authorize a large refactor, implementation session, deployment, or data migration.

## User-visible outcome

Several independent personas can use one standalone Laputa/Garden installation and the same underlying memory source:

- **Independent personalities:** select/connect persona A or B, with its own existing Persona/ACTMEM authority and correctly bound sessions. Switching personas must not mix their identities or memories.
- **Private by default:** A's ordinary conversations and captured memories remain private to A. Being in the same installation or workspace does not make B's private information visible.
- **Explicit, useful sharing:** the human creates/selects a named shared space and chooses which personas can read or contribute. Authorized personas can actually find and use shared information through their normal memory paths.
- **Understandable controls:** reuse existing UI/API surfaces to show the active persona, a memory's private/shared location, shared-space participants and access level. Support removing a participant. No separate enterprise administration console is required.

Example: A and B keep separate personal conversations, but both can recall the project decisions deliberately placed in shared space S. A third persona C cannot see S until added. Removing B stops new service-authorized reads of S; it cannot make B forget text already delivered.

## Minimal design direction

**Prefer exact Scope + a small shared-space membership/permission map, resolved by Garden.** Avoid a general IAM engine, per-record ACL framework or self-contained capability-token system in the first release.

Reuse existing identifiers and single-persona services. Current code treats `ProfileID` as the stable subject; do not redefine it as a tenant, rename the identity model, or require a new Profile/Subject/Agent hierarchy merely to follow the earlier proposal. Resolve an authenticated agent binding to the correct existing persona/subject. Settle any genuinely necessary contract delta before implementation.

The logical model needs only:

| Concept | First-release responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Trusted agent/persona binding | Identify the actual caller and its existing persona/subject. Request-body IDs are not permission grants. |
| Private scope | Reuse subject-private and subject/workspace-private exact scopes. Workspace membership alone never grants access to another persona's private scope. |
| Shared space | One explicitly identified resource scope, with owner-controlled membership and read or read/write access. Read does not imply write or permission management. Do not expose unrestricted cross-private-domain grants in the MVP. |
| Memory record | Reuse canonical identity, scope, revision, status and provenance. No duplicate memory authority or per-agent copy of shared memory. |

Use the smallest compatible representation for shared scopes. The earlier suggested `scope/v2`, new table roster, permission revision fields and access-view types are implementation candidates, not mandatory additions. Unknown/unclassified scope must remain non-public. Existing private data is not automatically reclassified.

Garden owns the access decision. Mentle remains the sole canonical source for stored memory and owns its revisions, receipts and derived indexes. Laputa retains Persona/ACTMEM semantics. Reuse existing Garden control-plane persistence for membership if persistence changes are needed; do not add a second memory database, separate authorization service or mirrored ACL authority inside every backend.

Keep the existing `Backend.Search`, `Expand`, `Mutate` and `MutationStatus` contracts wherever sufficient. A trusted Garden resolver can produce the admitted read scopes and bound write target. Multiple bound views should share the existing memory service/resources rather than start a full independent memory stack for each persona.

## Keep / change only where needed for the product contract

**Keep:** exact scope matching; trusted bound-client behavior; card-before-evidence reads; expected revisions; scoped writes/deletes; canonical transaction receipts and index outbox; existing UI, context and ingestion infrastructure.

**Required closure, not an optional hardening project:**

1. Bind each supported entrypoint to the actual persona. On multi-persona agent-facing surfaces, a shared role token, caller-supplied identity or loopback address alone must not grant access to every persona's data. Reuse trusted host handles or a minimal per-agent credential binding; do not introduce a full identity provider.
2. Route enabled search, evidence expansion, automatic bootstrap/recall and context assembly through the same Garden access decision. Scope/status/revision checks must protect the actual data returned, including with stale indexes. A safe explicit search is insufficient if automatic context bypasses it.
3. Preserve the originating subject and write scope in capture, queued work, spool/retry and restart paths. Bind persona snapshots and session state to their real owner. Reuse existing durable and idempotent mechanisms rather than inventing another ledger.
4. Human-selected sharing is explicit. Ordinary capture, Recap/persona updates and automatic summarization must not publish private material into shared spaces. First release may support explicitly writing selected information into a shared space without supporting in-place movement/publication of existing private records; disclose that limitation rather than silently copying/reclassifying records.
5. Removing membership must affect new authorized requests. Use simple re-resolution/invalidation for existing caches or handles; advanced policy-cache infrastructure is not required. Do not re-inject Garden-managed stale shared material as newly authorized context. Previously delivered external transcripts cannot be recalled.
6. All enabled data-bearing surfaces must respect visibility, including metadata and linked evidence. Optional graph/timeline, trace or global enumeration surfaces that cannot meet this cheaply may remain explicitly unavailable to multi-persona agents. Do not rewrite every optional subsystem as an MVP dependency.

A trusted single-owner/local deployment is the initial target. This is not hostile multi-tenant hosting or a sandbox for arbitrary malicious code. Agents with unrestricted filesystem, database or administrator access are outside the API isolation guarantee; do not advertise protection against those bypasses.

## Optional and deferred, not first-release blockers

- Per-record ACLs, nested groups, role inheritance, arbitrary cross-private-scope grants and a generic policy language.
- Signed/self-contained capability tokens, token attenuation/delegation chains, external IAM, multi-process/distributed authorization consistency and a dedicated permission service.
- Strict timing/statistical non-interference, mandatory vector-index partitioning or an index rewrite solely to obtain native pre-filtering. Authorization filtering before disclosure and usable recall are still required. Evaluate representative private/shared corpora; address an actual recall failure with the smallest change rather than claiming larger candidate pools prove isolation or completeness.
- Run-wide information-flow/taint tracking, automatic declassification approvals, prevention of all model paraphrasing/redistribution, and guaranteed erasure of already delivered context. Avoid autonomous private-to-shared publication in the MVP instead of building this machinery first.
- Full retroactive purge, cross-store cascading deletion, per-agent encryption/key management, hostile-plugin/process sandboxing and comprehensive audit/compliance dashboards.
- In-place publication/reclassification of existing private records, complex shared editing roles, independent graph/timeline isolation and advanced sharing management, unless a concrete first-release user workflow makes one necessary.

These are optional follow-ups, not promised phase-two delivery. Reopen an item only for a confirmed user need, reproduced failure or measured limitation. Add no new caches, concurrency layers, services or plugin frameworks without such evidence. Avoid silently removing existing capabilities from single-persona deployments while restricting unsupported multi-persona surfaces.

## Focused acceptance

- [ ] In one standalone installation and one canonical memory source, A/B have distinct persona and private-memory behavior; switching and restarting do not cross-bind identities or snapshots.
- [ ] With no sharing grant, A cannot obtain B's private content through enabled search, evidence, bootstrap/recall, context injection or exposed metadata. Conflicting caller-supplied bindings cannot grant access.
- [ ] A/B can find and use information in S after explicit membership; C cannot. UI/API shows the real scope and participants. Read-only members cannot mutate/delete records or grant access; authorized writes retain existing revision/conflict behavior.
- [ ] Removing B blocks subsequent service-authorized access, including via an old evidence ID/cursor or Garden-managed cached material. State the boundary for already delivered external context; do not claim retroactive forgetting.
- [ ] Capture, retry/restart and authorized update/delete preserve subject, scope, idempotency and canonical/index consistency. No silent cross-persona writes, shared publication, backend fallback or duplicate shared-memory store.
- [ ] Representative Chinese private/shared queries remain useful on supported lexical/vector paths. Record genuine limitations; no unsupported performance or completeness claims. Inspect actual model inputs, not only one API response field.
- [ ] Existing single-persona VIVY/DIVA behavior remains within its own contract. Reuse the conformance corpus and add only tests needed for these concrete failure paths; optional hardening is not a release gate.

Deliver the smallest end-to-end private/shared-memory slice before expanding optional surfaces. Stop when the product contract and these focused tests are covered.

## VIVY boundary and related ownership

This issue is for **standalone Laputa multi-persona composition**, not a multi-personality roster inside VIVY.

- [VIVY #57](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/57): one continuous VIVY subject, its persistent sessions and bounded role-only workers. A worker does not become an independent persona or inherit persona/Recap by default.
- [VIVY #58](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/agent-vivy/issues/58): one subject-level Recap and unified context admission, LIFE-first with CODE excluded from phase-one resident admission. A memory grant is not automatic context injection. This issue does not redefine ACTMEM schema or rollout policy.
- [Laputa #1](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/issues/1): existing embeddable-library and integration ownership; reuse those foundations.
- [Laputa #7](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/issues/7): Mentle enhancements. Do not make the full enhancement backlog a prerequisite for persona sharing.

## Source baseline for implementation review

Prior static review used `4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24`. These references are inspection starting points, not runtime-test certification. Refresh the touched paths before implementation; no code/tests were changed or run when filing this issue.

- [Exact Scope encoding](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/memory/scope.go), [Backend contract](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/memory/contract.go).
- [Identity binding](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/agentapi/contract.go), [role policy](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/agentapi/policy.go), [HTTP authentication](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/internal/server/auth.go).
- [Explicit reads](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/agentapi/reads.go), [runtime composition](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/internal/runtimecore/runtime.go), [automatic recall](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/internal/recall/fast.go), [Mentle adapter](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/backends/mentle/adapter.go).
- [Frozen sessions](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/internal/personactx/frozen.go), [capture/recovery](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/4b2bec2cc2ab3374b7ec1ab8d448e612c1e4db24/garden/internal/ingest/service.go).

author: mastwet

title: fix(actmem): do not poison the Recap owner when recovery is canceled …
body:
…before replacement

A canceled or expired context during first-use recovery marked the owner commit-unknown, so every later Recap read and write failed until the process restarted, although no head replacement had been attempted. Only a failure after a replacement starts (already marked inside publishRecapHead) or a non-context recovery error keeps that mark.

Also declare golang.org/x/sys as the direct dependency it is on Windows.

title: 架构重定位：Laputa 人格与记忆治理规范及 Garden 原生适配闭环
body:
## 背景与目标

新 Vivy 已经接入完整的 MemPalace 能力，Laputa 没有必要为了接入再复制一套长期记忆引擎。我们希望按“多、快、好、省”重新裁剪 Laputa：保留人格治理和演化的价值，同时让不同 Agent 可以复用其规范与工作流。

目标是将 Laputa 定位为**人格与记忆治理的规范和协议**，具体实现贴合宿主 Agent。Garden 提供可复用的语料收集、更新和治理工作流，也可以在后续提供统一管理入口。

## 方向

- **人格**：明确人格的权威来源、读取和修改方式，以及注入人格上下文的边界。新 Vivy 倾向使用精简的 Rust 原生实现，在主 Agent 的提示词中提供人格根层。
- **长期记忆**：由可替换的引擎负责。新 Vivy 当前使用完整的 MemPalace；将来可以研究 Mem0 等后端，协议不应把某一种引擎或数据格式变成普遍前提。替换不等于自动具备数据迁移或能力等价。
- **短期 Recap**：优先由 Agent 或其 harness 负责。规范说明所有权及接入方式，复用宿主现有的上下文、压缩和持久化机制。
- **Garden 闭环**：收集语料/证据 → 调用选定的 Agent 或宿主已有演化流程 → 生成候选更新 → 按宿主的写入策略应用 → 检查持久化和实际生效状态 → 保存结果与必要证据。候选生成本身不是闭环完成。
- **原生适配**：针对 Hermes、OpenClaw 等 Agent，先研究其现有的人格文件、记忆与自主进化机制，优先更新已有权威文件或使用其支持的接口，避免建立第二套人格副本或互相竞争的演化链路。
- **新 Vivy 的 AutoDream**：延续此前决策，候选更新通过演化链路自动采纳，不以逐项人工审核作为常态。其他宿主遵循各自的写入策略。
- Garden Web 控制台及其未来管理 Vivy 内部 Laputa 的方式保留为后续讨论。

## 与现有架构的协调

本次讨论稿已上传至 [设计分支及决策记录](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/48ec533a076fe868b21afacdfde2b598eea97c6d/docs/architecture/0016-laputa-protocol-and-native-agent-governance.md)。它基于较早的本地快照，**尚未合并到最新 main**。

远端 main 已包含 [ADR-0016：可嵌入模块化单体](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/main/docs/architecture/0016-laputa-embeddable-modular-monolith.md)、ADR-0017 和 [ADR-0018：VIVY 上下文与 Recap 策略](https://github.com/ProjectViVy/laputa/blob/main/docs/architecture/0018-vivy-unified-context-and-recap-policy.md)。整理进主线前需要：

1. 在最新 main 上重新整理设计稿，避免 ADR 编号冲突，并逐项说明对 ADR-0016/0017/0018 的继承、调整与待决问题。
2. 区分已有 Go 实现的合同和可跨宿主复用的规范；保留已验证实现作为证据，不把它直接当成新架构已完成。
3. 明确与宿主原生 Recap、现有角色/权限边界及人格修改策略的关系；不要为统一接口制造第二套权威数据。
4. 检查现有未提交工作区的改动，在不覆盖这些改动的前提下推进设计和后续实现。

## 待设计和验证

- 最小规范包含哪些语义，哪些属于宿主适配器；是否需要网络传输及其形式。
- 人格表示、读写和权限、并发冲突、版本/历史、运行中何时加载新状态。
- 后端能力发现与不支持操作的表达；长期记忆替换和迁移是否需要另立项目。
- 语料范围、Agent 调用、失败恢复、重复执行、更新回读，以及宿主已经内置演化链路时如何复用。
- 选择一个真实宿主完成最小纵向验证，再决定公共 SDK、Web 控制台和其他适配器的范围。

本 issue 记录架构方向和后续工作；不代表这些适配、后端替换或工作流已经实现。
